answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable deposit and earn reputation through repeated trades with independently trusted peers. Random challenges ask an account to sign fresh messages tied to its prior history, so copied identities cannot cheaply share one nontransferable record. Coordinated newborn agents produce a ripple of conflicting attestations, lose their deposits, and must restart the voyage. A pigment-coded audit trail makes those resets visible, forcing the attacker to pay capital and time for every replacement.
